subject: Banking
title: The Panic of 1907
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Panic of 1907.

hook.text: Two speculators tried to corner the copper market in 1907. When they failed, the banks that funded them collapsed.

buildup.text: When Knickerbocker Trust failed, panic spread fast and depositors rushed to pull cash across New York.

discovery.text: J.P. Morgan organized a rescue. He locked bankers in his library until they agreed to pool funds and stop the panic.

twist.text: Morgan profited from the rescue by buying assets at distressed prices. The savior was also the biggest winner.

climax.text: One private banker saving the financial system proved the need for a central bank.

punchline.text: Morgan saved the system and profited from it.

quiz.question: What did the Panic of 1907 lead to?
options: The creation of the Federal Reserve

details.summary: The Panic of 1907 was a severe financial crisis in the United States where a failed speculation attempt triggered cascading bank runs. J.P. Morgan personally organized a private rescue that stabilized the system and inspired the creation of the Federal Reserve.
details.whyItMatters: The Panic of 1907 demonstrated that a modern economy could not rely on one private individual to prevent financial collapse. The crisis directly led to the creation of the Federal Reserve System in 1913.
takeaways: A failed attempt to corner United Copper stock triggered the panic
J.P. Morgan locked bankers in his library until they agreed to a rescue
The crisis led directly to the creation of the Federal Reserve in 1913

faq.question: How did J.P. Morgan stop the panic?
faq.answer: Morgan assessed which institutions were solvent and organized pools of money from banks and wealthy individuals to provide emergency loans. He famously locked bankers in his library and refused to let them leave until they agreed to participate.

faq.question: How did the panic lead to the Federal Reserve?
faq.answer: The reliance on one private citizen to save the financial system was clearly unsustainable. Congress concluded that the country needed a permanent central bank that could provide emergency liquidity and regulate the banking system systematically.
